prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Conservative Party Manifesto 2015 – Summary (≤500 words)

Core aim: Secure a stronger economy and improve life “at every stage,” funded by fiscal discipline and pro-enterprise policies.

Economy, tax and welfare
- Eliminate the deficit, then run a surplus; no rises in VAT, Income Tax or National Insurance.
- Raise Personal Allowance to £12,500 and the 40p threshold to £50,000; create a “Tax‑Free Minimum Wage” link so full‑time minimum‑wage earners pay no Income Tax.
- Crack down on tax evasion/avoidance; make the Office of Tax Simplification permanent.
- Reform welfare: lower the household benefit cap to £23,000; freeze most working‑age benefits for two years; roll out Universal Credit; replace JSA for 18–21s with a time‑limited Youth Allowance tied to work/training; restrict Housing Benefit for most 18–21s.

Jobs, business and skills
- Create 2 million more jobs; achieve full employment.
- Support small firms via a business rates review, reduced red tape (£10bn cut), Start Up Loans expansion, faster public procurement for SMEs.
- Deliver 3 million new apprenticeships; abolish employers’ NICs for apprentices under 25.
- Invest in science/innovation (catapults, Eight Great Technologies) and £6.9bn research infrastructure.

NHS and social care
- Increase NHS spending every year; at least £8bn more by 2020 to fund the Five Year Forward View.
- Seven‑day GP access and hospital care by 2020; same‑day GP appointments for over‑75s; integrated health and social care (Better Care Fund).
- Prioritise mental health (access/waiting standards), cancer care (Cancer Drugs Fund), and dementia; cap residential care costs.

Education
- Protect per‑pupil funding; pupil premium maintained; at least 500 new free schools; convert failing/coasting schools to academies.
- Tougher primary standards; core academic GCSEs; more maths/science (17,500 extra maths/physics teachers).
- No cap on university places; postgraduate loans; more degree apprenticeships; improve FE and National Colleges.

Housing and planning
- Build 200,000 Starter Homes (20% discount for under‑40 first‑time buyers); extend Help to Buy (equity loans, mortgage guarantee, Help to Buy ISA).
- Extend Right to Buy to housing association tenants; fund replacements; prioritise brownfield; protect the Green Belt.

Infrastructure and connectivity
- Over £100bn capital investment; £38bn for rail (HS2/HS3, electrification, Crossrail/2); freeze regulated commuter fares in real terms.
- £15bn for roads; cycling investment; superfast broadband to 95% by end‑2017; push ultrafast and 90% mobile landmass coverage.

Immigration and EU
- Aim to reduce net migration to tens of thousands; four‑year residency for EU in‑work benefits and social housing; tougher enforcement and removals; tackle illegal working and trafficking.
- Hold an in‑out EU referendum by end‑2017; keep the pound; seek EU reform, protect the Single Market, scrap the Human Rights Act and introduce a British Bill of Rights.

Energy and environment
- Keep bills down via competition and smart meters by 2020; support shale, nuclear and cost‑effective renewables; end new subsidies for onshore wind; support CCS.
- Plant 11m trees; protect Green Belt; create a “Blue Belt” of marine conservation; invest in flood defences; improve air and water quality.

Crime, security and defence
- Continue police reform, tackle cybercrime, toughen sentences, introduce a Victims’ Law, target violence against women and girls, restrict psychoactive substances.
- Maintain Armed Forces (Army ≥82,000); renew Trident; meet NATO commitments; invest £160bn in equipment; support veterans; spend 0.7% GNI on international development.

Pensions and retirees
- Maintain the triple lock; introduce single‑tier pension; preserve pensioner benefits; expand pension freedoms; raise effective Inheritance Tax threshold on the family home to £1m; cap care costs.

Devolution and governance
- English votes for English laws; implement new powers for Scotland (Smith) and Wales (St David’s Day); support the Stormont House Agreement.
- Cut government waste, increase transparency, modernise public services, and expand National Citizen Service and volunteering leave.
